title: Keepers of the Holy Land
hookLine: brown-robed friars who keep watch over the places of Jesus's life, and the walk they brought home

lines: A BROWN HABIT, A ROPE BELT.
HE ISN'T VISITING. HE LIVES THERE.
cards: A brown habit. A rope belt with knots in it. Sandals.
That outfit belongs to Assisi, to Francis and his brothers. But you can also meet it in the stone streets of Jerusalem, Bethlehem and Nazareth, on a friar who isn't visiting. He lives there.

He sweeps a shrine, unlocks a door for pilgrims at dawn, and sings the hours in a chapel built over a place from the Gospels. Tradition says the brothers of Francis have kept watch over these places for centuries.
Today, those keepers, and the walk they carried home.

teach.b: Back on day one hundred fifty, you met the Stations; today, the friars behind them. They call their charge the Custody of the Holy Land, and the brother who leads them is the Custos, the keeper.
The job is plain and endless: care for the shrines, pray in them, and welcome pilgrims with sore feet. Some of the holiest places aren't theirs alone.

teach.h: HOLY PLACES SHARED WITH OTHER CHURCHES.
teach.b: The church over Calvary and the empty tomb is shared by several Christian churches, Orthodox and Armenian and others alongside the Catholics, each with its own corners and hours.
So keeping the Holy Land means keeping the peace in it.
Then there's the walk. In Jerusalem, pilgrims wanted to follow the road Jesus took to the cross, stopping to pray. Luke tells one of those stops.

Women follow him, weeping, and he turns to them. In the Douay-Rheims: "Daughters of Jerusalem, weep not over me; but weep for yourselves, and for your children." But not everyone can get to that street.

teach.h: THE WALK CARRIED HOME TO EVERY PARISH.
teach.b: So the walk was carried home. The friars helped spread the Stations of the Cross, crosses or pictures on a church wall, so a grandmother in a village could walk the road to Calvary in her own parish.

teach.h: DAUGHTERS OF JERUSALEM, WEEP NOT OVER ME.
teach.b: A surprise on that wall: some stops come straight from the Gospels, like Simon of Cyrene taking up the cross, and some from tradition, like Veronica wiping his face. The Gospels never mention her.
The Stations hold both, and the friars kept both.

how: Catholics pray the Stations of the Cross in parish churches, especially on the Fridays of Lent, walking or turning from one station to the next; in Jerusalem, Franciscan friars lead the walk through the streets of the old city.

games.q: what does “keepers of the holy land” mean?
o: crusader knights who guarded pilgrims on the roads
the bishops who govern the churches of Jerusalem
Franciscan friars who care for the shrines of Jesus's life

p: the friar who leads the custody
a stop that comes from the Gospels
a stop that comes from tradition

s: the friars keep the church of the tomb all by themselves
several Christian churches share it, Orthodox and Armenian among them, each with its own corners and hours.
every stop on the Stations of the Cross comes from the Gospels
some do, like Simon of Cyrene. Veronica comes from tradition; the Gospels never mention her.
the Stations were spread so people far from Jerusalem could walk the road too
the walk was carried home, so a village parish could follow the road to Calvary.

games.q: you long to walk the road Jesus took to the cross, but you will never get to Jerusalem. what do you do?
o: give up: it only counts in Jerusalem.
send someone else to walk it for you.
walk the Stations on your own parish church's walls.
games.why: that's what the Stations are for. the friars helped carry Jerusalem's walk home, so anyone could take it in their own church.

practice: Stand if you can, take a few slow steps and stop, and bring to mind Jesus handed over to die; a few more steps, and Simon, a stranger pulled from the crowd to carry the cross; a few more, and the women on the road, and the words he said to them.
If you pray, say an Our Father at the last stop; if not, just stand still and let the road be quiet.

wordCard.voice: Keepers of the Holy Land. The friars in brown who care for the places of Jesus's life, and who helped carry his road home to every parish. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin: the Custody of the Holy Land, the friars' name for their charge.

carryVoice: Your line: the custody. Some keep watch in Jerusalem, and the road comes home to every parish wall. See you tomorrow.

sources.q: Daughters of Jerusalem, weep not over me; but weep for yourselves, and for your children.
